## Career Pivots Are the New Normal

LinkedIn data shows that professionals now change careers (not just jobs) an average of 3 times during their working life. The stigma around career pivots has evaporated — but the practical challenges remain.

### Most Common Successful Pivots

| From | To | Transferable Skills | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Teaching | Corporate Training / L&D | Communication, curriculum design | 3-6 months |
| Military | Project Management | Leadership, operations, logistics | 2-4 months |
| Journalism | Content Marketing | Writing, research, storytelling | 1-3 months |
| Finance → FinTech | Product Management | Domain expertise, analytics | 4-8 months |
| Healthcare → Health Tech | Customer Success | Domain knowledge, empathy | 3-6 months |
| Retail Management | Operations Manager | People management, P&L | 2-4 months |

### The Pivot Framework

#### Step 1: Skills Audit (Week 1-2)

Map every skill you use in your current role. Most professionals undercount their transferable skills by 40%.

#### Step 2: Target Industry Research (Week 3-4)

Identify 3 target industries. For each, map the overlap between your skills and their requirements. Aim for 60%+ overlap.

#### Step 3: Bridge the Gap (Month 2-4)

Take certifications, side projects, or volunteer work to demonstrate new-industry competence. One portfolio project is worth more than three certifications.

#### Step 4: Network and Position (Month 3-5)

Reach out to people who have made similar pivots. Their referrals carry weight because they can vouch for the transition pattern.

#### Step 5: Apply Strategically (Month 4-6)

Target companies that value diverse backgrounds. Startups and mid-size companies are typically more open to career changers than enterprises.

### Compensation During a Pivot

Expect a 10-20% compensation dip in Year 1, with recovery by Year 2-3. This is a short-term investment for long-term career satisfaction and growth.
